newsitem.title: DUBAI: UNHCR seeks to move Kurdish camps from border.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR seeks to move Kurdish camps from border.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency said on Wednesday it was negotiating with Iran to relocate eight camps which shelter tens of thousands of Iraqi Kurds further away from the Iran-Iraq border.
"One of our major concerns is the relocation issue," Laurens Jolles, a spokesman for the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Tehran told Reuters by telephone.

The eight camps, now home to 43,000 refugees who fled from the takeover of northern Iraq by the Baghdad-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party, are all within seven km (four miles) of the border and one is as close as 500 metres yards).
More refugees were still arriving at the border camps, Jolles said.
Relocation of the camps was necessary to ensure refugees' safety from cross-border attacks and to help the distribution of food and medicine by aid agencies, he said.
Eleven Iraqi Kurds were killed and 35 wounded in cross-border shooting at one camp in northwestern Iran on September 18.
The UNHCR says it usually prefers refugee camps holding people fleeing persecution or civil war to be located at least 50 km (30 miles) from a frontier.
